title: A planet hunter and its neighbor
caption: Orion over the ESO 3.6-meter telescope walkway, La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The constellation of Orion, the Hunter, looks down on a small walkway at ESO's La Silla Observatory. The walkway links the ESO 3.6-meter telescope with the Coudé Auxiliary Telescope, which is no longer in use.

This long exposure by ESO Photo Ambassador Yuri Beletsky hides several details. On the right, a streak of light marks an artificial satellite passing behind the telescope dome. A faint reddish arc curves around the bright Orion Nebula. This is Barnard's Loop, an emission nebula thought to be what remains of a supernova, the explosion of a star. Just below the walkway and running alongside it, the dark dust lanes of the Milky Way ripple across the stars.
The 3.6-meter telescope carries HARPS, the High Accuracy Radial velocity Planet Searcher, counted among the most accurate and productive planet-hunting instruments astronomy has ever had.

understand.summary: This is a long-exposure landscape photograph taken with a camera at La Silla, in visible light. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: The long exposure gathers much more light than the eye, revealing the faint red arc of Barnard's Loop and recording the passing satellite as a streak.

explore: HARPS, as its full name suggests, hunts for planets by measuring radial velocity, the tiny shifts in a star's motion toward and away from us caused by the pull of orbiting planets.
alt: The constellation Orion above a walkway between two telescope buildings, with a faint red arc around a bright nebula, a satellite streak on the right and dark Milky Way dust below.
